subject: Data flight paths and subprocessor routing — Q&A
messages:
From: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@stratamed.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Data Protection Team <dataprotection@stratamed.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Oct 2028 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q on where requests run (regions & subprocessors)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team wants a succinct answer to two items before we take this into procurement:

1) Where will StrataMed customer inference payloads be executed by default for our US tenants? Are there any common transient hops outside the US (cloud providers, queueing, monitoring services)?
2) Which subprocessors might touch inference payloads (logging, monitoring, metrics, alerting) and are any of those vendors outside the US?

Can you point us to a single slide or short attachment we can include in our internal memo? If you can also call out the deletion/retention commitments for cached KV/short-term telemetry, that would help.

Best,
Aisha Malik
Head of IT Risk | StrataMed

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@stratamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where requests run (regions & subprocessors)

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: for US tenants requests are executed in US cloud regions by default; transient telemetry and routing control-plane metadata may traverse additional regions for health checks and autoscaling signals but payloads and KV caches are kept within US-regional compute unless you choose a geo-restricted private deployment.

I attached a concise appendix that covers: primary execution regions, common transient hops (edge load balancers, control-plane metrics), and a high-level subprocessor roster with country loci. Key points: 
- Default execution: US East (primary) and US West (failover) across our cloud provider partners.
- Prefix/KV cache: encrypted, stored in-region, TTL default 1 hour for session caches (configurable).
- Control-plane telemetry: aggregated and pushed to monitoring endpoints; metadata for orchestration may use vendor-managed control-plane services which are contractually restricted from accessing payload contents.

I've also attached a spreadsheet snapshot of our current subprocessor inventory (non-exhaustive; we provide SOC2 evidence and contractual terms on request).

Next steps I propose: 1) quick 20-min call with your DP team to walk the appendix; 2) if you want us to produce a short 1‑page memo for procurement, we can generate that with explicit contract clause references.

Attachments: redwood-data-flightpaths-appendix.pdf (pdf), subprocessor-inventory-2028-10.xlsx (xlsx)

—
Jordan Blake

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 4 Oct 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where requests run (regions & subprocessors)

Aisha — adding a couple of clarifications from the Compliance team so your reviewers don't have to parse the appendix: 

1) Transient Hops: 
   • Edge/Load-balancing: TLS-terminating load balancers may be in a nearby region to reduce latency; we require TLS >=1.2 and do not persist payloads at the edge.
   • Control-plane signals: autoscaler heartbeats and instance lifecycle events may route through our control-plane region which is logically separate from execution; those messages contain metrics/IDs only and never the inference prompt or response text.

2) Subprocessors: 
   • Observability vendors (metrics/alerting): only receive anonymized operational telemetry by default; full content is not shipped to third-party monitoring.
   • Logging: request/response bodies are not sent to external logging vendors in hosted mode. We retain request metadata (timestamps, model id, token counts) per your chosen retention policy.

3) Deletion/Retention: 
   • Short-term KV/prefix caches: default TTL 1 hour; customer can set to a minimum of 30 minutes or disable.
   • Audit/usage metadata: default retention 90 days for self-serve accounts; enterprise plans can request custom retention windows and export/archival via our secure transfer process.

If helpful we can produce a redlineable clause for procurement that states: "Runtime execution of customer inference requests for US tenants will be limited to US regional compute unless otherwise agreed in writing." Let me know and we can draft.

—
Marissa Cole
Director, Compliance | Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@stratamed.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@stratamed.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Data Protection Team <dataprotection@stratamed.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Oct 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where requests run (regions & subprocessors)

Thanks Jordan & Marissa — that is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple quick follow-ups from our DP team before procurement: 

1) Can you confirm whether any of the named subprocessors in the spreadsheet have sub-subprocessors outside the US that process metadata (not content)? If yes, can you identify which vendors and countries?
2) For the deletion commitments: will you include a clause in the SOW that the default KV cache TTL is configurable and that Redwood will delete ephemeral caches on contract termination within 30 days?

If you can answer those two items in writing we can clear the compliance blocker. If it's easier, we'll take the 20-minute call.

Appreciate it — Liam
Data Protection Lead | StrataMed
